review_notes: I read the whole file and checked each new definition for overlap with Mathlib. The new definitions are `phi`, `phiM`, `rad`, `Cong`, `glEquiv` and `atPlace`, all private. `phi` is `MulAut.conj δ` composed with `sigmaGL`, and `phiM` is built from `AddMonoidHom.mulLeft`, `AddMonoidHom.mulRight` and `mapMatrix`. `glEquiv` and `atPlace` are assembled from `Units.mapEquiv`, `Matrix.piRingEquiv`, `MulEquiv.piUnits` and `Pi.evalMonoidHom`. These all reuse Mathlib constructions, so they are not competing versions. `rad` is the set of elements of the semilocal tensor product whose valuation is below 1 at every place above v. `Cong` is the matrix congruence modulo `rad` scaled by ν. I did not find a Mathlib definition with the same meaning for a product of valuations over a tensor algebra. Mathlib's single-valuation `ltAddSubgroup` does not cover the product case. The private lemmas about `rad`, `semiLocalHomeomorph`, `mul_mem_integralUnitsSet` and `pow_finrank_eq_one` are theorem-level work, which the rubric excludes. The `integralUnitsSet` and `semiLocalIntegralSet` definitions live in other files, so I did not treat them as introduced here. The main uncertainty is that I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for a Pi-valuation radical or ideal.
